name: Madrasso
description: Madrasso is a classic Venetian trick-taking game played in partnerships. It is a member of the 'Tressette' family but features a trump suit, making it a bridge between Tressette and Briscola. Known for its specific point target (777 points) and the 'exchange' of the trump indicator card, it is the quintessential game of the Veneto region of Italy. It requires careful hand management and a strong memory of point-cards already played.

history.origins: Developed in the 18th century as a variation of Tressette that introduced the 'Atout' (Trump) as a permanent feature.
timeline: 1700s: Madrasso (and the verb 'madrassare') enters the Venetian dialect.
1900s: Becomes a staple in Venice's city clubs and rural taverns.
Present: Still the most played partnership game in the Venice-Padua-Treviso triangle.
2012: The 'Associazione Madrasso' publishes standardized tournament rules.
history.cultural: In Venice, it is traditional to play Madrasso in pairs for an 'Ombra' (a small glass of wine).
history.evolution: The game's 777-point target is symbolic, intended to create a long session of at least 10 rounds where consistent play is rewarded over 1-round luck.

setup.players: 4 players in two partnerships (North-South vs East-West).
setup.deck: 40 cards: Ace (11), 3 (10), King (4), Knight (3), Jack (2), and 7-6-5-4-2 (0). Total points = 120 + 10 for last trick.
setup.dealing: Each player is dealt 10 cards. The 21st card is turned face-up as the Trump Indicator.

rules.objective: Win the game by being the first partnership to reach 777 points over at least 10 deals (battute), counting points from tricks and the 10-point bonus for the last trick; or win immediately by taking all 10 tricks in one deal (cappotto).
rules.gameplay: 1. Must follow suit if possible. 2. If void, you can play a trump or discard any card. 3. The highest card of the led suit wins, unless a trump is played (Highest trump wins). 4. Winner of trick leads next.
keyRules: Must try to win the trick if possible (Overtake)
If unable to follow suit, must play a trump card if available
Winner of the trick leads the next

strategy.basic: Prioritize the Ace and 3. In Madrasso, these two cards alone account for 21 out of 30 point-value in a suit. If you have the Ace of Trump, you are the master of the table.
strategy.intermediate: The Seven Switch: Don't always swap the 7 for the King or Knight indicator immediately if you want to hide your trump strength. However, if the indicator is the Ace or 3, swap it as soon as possible!
strategy.advanced: Partner Lead-Deduction: If your partner leads a small Diamond, they likely have either the Diamond Ace or no trump. If they lead a Trump, they are 'draining' the opponents of high cards to protect their own 3s in side suits.
tips: Memory: You must track which Aces and 3s have been played. If the Ace of Cups is gone, your 3 of Cups is the highest card.
Winning the 10th trick is essentialâ€”it's worth as much as a King and 6 points combined.
